title: My Fortune Cookie Was BLANK 🥠
premise: At the gas station on our highway every fortune cookie comes true by Friday, word for word. A man finds forty dollars in his tire, geese follow a woman for a week. Every Wednesday my grandpa Ike and I fill up his truck and read our fortunes out loud. Last Wednesday mine was blank, and the clerk had only seen one blank before.
twist: A blank is the one fortune you get to write, and it comes true for whoever you hand it to. The other blank was Grandpa's, fifty years ago: he wrote it for Grandma, 'You will never eat dinner alone', and he has never missed one. I write mine for him, 'You will never fill up your truck alone', and now I fill his tank every week.
world: a bright highway gas station with two red pumps under a white canopy and a teal pickup, a shop with a jar of wrapped cookies, and Grandpa's small yellow kitchen with Grandma's green armchair through the doorway
